matches.rationale: Finding 1 identifies the same core contradiction in the Abstract: ALFAR is described as training-free and plug-and-play while also involving light training/fine-tuning, which matches the ground-truth corruption about inconsistent claims of whether ALFAR requires additional training.
No finding addresses the asymmetric logits fusion formula in Equation (11) or the risk of negative weights/inversion effects.
No finding mentions the asymmetry in GPU resources or batch sizes between ALFAR and baseline methods.
Finding 2 concerns a nonsensical caption sentence about reduced gains, not the corruption of inflated ALFAR accuracy numbers in Tables 2 and 3.
No finding discusses overclaimed qualitative example accuracy or the failure to acknowledge ambiguous/incorrect responses in the discussion.
No finding addresses missing IRB approvals, consent procedures, or privacy safeguards in the acknowledgments/appendices.
No finding identifies future-dated or fabricated references such as [12], [27], or [41].
No finding discusses promotional rhetoric in the Introduction overstating ALFAR's effectiveness without appropriate caveats.
No finding notes the inconsistency between text next to Figure 1 and the plotted 2nd/3rd retrieved-knowledge performance.
No finding addresses heterogeneous baseline models lacking normalization or the resulting comparison bias.

Finding 5 notes a figure-text mismatch about InstructBLIP 13B decline, but does not identify the cross-section contradiction between claimed scalability/overhead and the observed performance decline across model scales.
No finding mentions missing bias or safety evaluations for the knowledge bases in the experimental setup.
Finding 4 concerns misattribution of GPT-3.5 to an InstructGPT paper, not the GPT-4 technical report reference [71] cited as an arXiv preprint.
No finding addresses the Conclusion's selective rhetoric omitting previously discussed limitations.
No finding discusses related-work citation bias or the neglect of existing training-free fusion methods.
Finding 3 concerns the absence of retrieval-similarity α in the attention reallocation equations, not the failure to preserve causal masks or autoregressive constraints.
